verdict.reasoning: Patient states, 'I just feel I can't really hear as well as I used to, like my hearing is kind of deteriorating,' indicating reduced hearing.
Duration: Patient reports reduced hearing 'about six weeks.' Side: When asked, 'is that both ears or just the left ear?' patient replies, 'Uh just the left ear, yeah.'

Patient says, 'I occasionally get like a ringing in my left ear... it's kind of on and off. Like some things trigger it as well. So, for example, if I'm watching TV or listen to music or something that'll solve the ringing in the ear,' which describes intermittent left-sided tinnitus influenced by TV/music.

Patient notes 'a few times when I felt kind of a bit sick or a bit dizzy as well' and later clarifies, 'nothing major... not proper room spinning... but just, just a little bit kind of off balance,' consistent with occasional mild dizziness and feeling off-balance.

Pain: Doctor asks, 'have you had any pain from the ear at all?' Patient responds, 'Uh no my left ear.' Discharge: Doctor asks, 'Any discharge coming out of the ear? No, OK.' Fever: Doctor asks, 'have you been experiencing any fever?' Patient replies, 'Uh, not specifically apart from the dizziness so much,' which is effectively a denial of fever.
Doctor asks, 'Have, have you had any chest pain with it?' Patient: 'No.' Doctor then asks, 'Any palpitations, heart beating fast?' and moves on without a positive response, implying no palpitations.
Doctor asks, 'do you use cotton ball buds to try and clean out wax from your ears?' Patient replies, 'Uh nah I'll do it,' followed by doctor, 'No, OK,' indicating patient does not use cotton buds.

Summarizes transcript data: left-sided hearing loss for six weeks (patient: 'about six weeks,' 'just the left ear'), intermittent tinnitus and mild disequilibrium/off-balance (as described), and no pain, discharge, or fever; doctor explicitly considers 'impacted wax, blocking the tube... which can lead to muffled hearing' versus 'a problem inside the drum or the balance system within the ear,' aligning with ruling out cerumen impaction versus middle/inner ear pathology.

Doctor states, 'maybe if we book you in for a face-to-face appointment in one of our clinics... within the next four, five days or so,' and notes need to 'have a look inside the ear drum' to check for 'physical blockage or whether there's something else going on,' consistent with otoscopy for wax/other otologic cause.

Doctor: 'I'll send a message to our admin team. I'll ask them to slot you into the clinic... Bear with me five minutes and then you can ring the support team, I'll leave the number in the notes for this appointment. Ring them, and then they'll slot you in,' which matches admin scheduling and patient calling support line.

Doctor says, 'What I might do... I'm going to, uh, put paste the link for a leaflet about Tinnitus, um, in the notes for this appointment. I'd really appreciate it if you could start reading about it,' which is providing a tinnitus education leaflet link for review before the clinic visit.

Doctor advises, 'If there's any problem, any issues between now and when the clinic appointment is, just book another appointment and you can speak to one of us over video,' which is safety-netting for earlier review if symptoms change or worsen.
